svg.text: Tang Nano 20K without the cache: LDA $0200 ; STA $0201 (copy one byte), code and data in the SDRAM

RTL trace (Verilator), read cache and posted writes off, 54 MHz, 1 clock = 18.5 ns. Every access to the SDRAM holds the 6809: one bus cycle = 41 clocks instead of 28 (the dead cycle has no access: 28).

SDRAM command: A = ACTIVE, R = READ (auto precharge), W = WRITE (auto precharge); the controller starts an access about 20 clocks into the cycle, the CPU is held 24 clocks for each access (read or write).

The two instructions make 8 SDRAM accesses (LDA: 3 fetches + 1 read, STA: 3 fetches + 1 write, 41 clocks each) and 2 dead cycles (28 each): 384 clocks; with the cache hits (code and data) they take 10 x 28 = 280.
Measured on the RTL of fpga/tn20k (Verilator), not on the board. Signals: soc.e, cpu_a, cpu_rnw, stall, ps_rd/ps_wr, ctl_busy, sd_ras_n/cas_n/we_n.
